In [[conformal geometry]], the '''tractor bundle''' is a particular [[vector bundle]] constructed on a [[conformal manifold]] whose fibres form an [[Group action (mathematics)|effective]] [[group representation|representation]] of the [[conformal group]]  (see [[associated bundle]]).  

The term ''tractor'' is a [[portmanteau]] of "Tracy Thomas" and "twistor", the bundle having been introduced first by [[Tracy Yerkes Thomas|T. Y. Thomas]] as an alternative formulation of the [[Cartan connection|Cartan]] [[conformal connection]],<ref>Thomas, T. Y., "On conformal differential geometry", ''Proc. N.A.S.'' '''12''' (1926), 352–359; "Conformal tensors", Proc. N.A.S. '''18''' (1931), 103–189.</ref> and later rediscovered within the formalism of [[local twistor]]s and generalized to [[projective connection]]s by [[Michael Eastwood]] ''et al.'' in <ref name="BaileyEastwoodGover">{{citation|author1=Bailey, T. N.|author2=Eastwood, M. G.|author3=Gover, A. R.|title=Thomas's structure bundle for conformal, projective and related structures|journal=Rocky Mountain J|volume=24|year=1994|pages=1191–1217|url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/rocky-mountain-journal-of-mathematics/volume-24/issue-4/Thomass-Structure-Bundle-for-Conformal-Projective-and-Related-Structures/10.1216/rmjm/1181072333.full}}</ref>  Tractor bundles can be defined for arbitrary [[parabolic geometry (differential geometry)|parabolic geometries]].<ref>Čap, A., & Gover, A. (2002). Tractor calculi for parabolic geometries. Transactions of the American Mathematical Society, 354(4), 1511-1548.</ref>

== Conformal manifolds ==
The tractor bundle for a <math>n</math>-dimensional conformal manifold <math>M</math> of signature <math>(p,q)</math> is a rank <math>n+2</math> vector bundle <math>\mathcal T\to M</math> equipped with the following data:<ref name="BaileyEastwoodGover"/>
* a metric <math>G:\mathcal T\otimes\mathcal T\to\mathbb R</math>, of signature <math>(p+1,q+1)</math>,
* a line subbundle <math>\mathcal X\subset\mathcal T</math>,
* a [[linear connection]] <math>\nabla</math>, preserving the metric <math>G</math>, and satisfying the nondegeneracy property that, for any local non-vanishing section <math>X</math> of the bundle <math>\mathcal X</math>,
<math display="block">v\mapsto \nabla_vX\pmod{\mathcal X}</math>
is a linear isomorphism at each point from the [[tangent bundle]] of <math>M</math> (<math>v\in TM</math>) to the quotient bundle <math>\mathcal X^\perp/\mathcal X</math>, where <math>\mathcal X^\perp</math> denotes the orthogonal complement of <math>\mathcal X</math> in <math>\mathcal T</math> relative to the metric <math>G</math>.

Given a tractor bundle, the metrics in the conformal class are given by fixing a local section <math>X</math> of <math>\mathcal X</math>, and defining for <math>v,w\in TM</math>,
<math display="block">g_X(v,w) = G(\nabla_vX,\nabla_wX).</math>

To go the other way, and construct a tractor bundle from a conformal structure, requires more work.  The tractor bundle is then an [[associated bundle]] of the Cartan geometry determined by the conformal structure.  The conformal group for a manifold of signature <math>(p,q)</math> is <math>SO(p+1,q+1)</math>, and one obtains the tractor bundle (with connection) as the connection induced by the Cartan conformal connection on the bundle associated to the standard representation of the conformal group.  Because the fibre of the Cartan conformal bundle is the stabilizer of a null ray, this singles out the line bundle <math>\mathcal X</math>.

More explicitly, suppose that <math>g</math> is a metric on <math>M</math>, with Levi-Civita connection <math>\nabla</math>.  The tractor bundle is the space of 2-jets of solutions <math>\sigma</math> to the eigenvalue equation
<math display="block">(\nabla_i\nabla_j + P_{ij})\sigma = \lambda g_{ij}</math>
where <math>P_{ij}</math> is the [[Schouten tensor]].  A little work then shows that the sections of the tractor bundle (in a fixed Weyl gauge) can be represented by <math>(n+2)</math>-vectors
<math display="block">U^I=\begin{bmatrix}\sigma\\ \mu^i\\ \rho\end{bmatrix}.</math>
The connection is 
<math display="block">\nabla_jU^I=\nabla_j\begin{bmatrix}\sigma\\ \mu^i\\ \rho\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_j\sigma-\mu_j\\ \nabla_j\mu^i + \delta_j^i\rho + P_j^i\sigma\\ \nabla_j\rho - P_{ji}\mu^i\end{bmatrix}.</math>
The metric, on <math>U^I=(\sigma\ \mu^i\ \rho)</math> and <math>V^J=(\tau\ \nu^j\ \alpha)</math> is:
<math display="block">G_{IJ}U^IV^J = \mu^i\nu_i + \sigma\tau + \rho\alpha</math>
The preferred line bundle <math>\mathcal X</math> is the span of
<math display="block">X^I = \begin{bmatrix}0\\0\\1\end{bmatrix}.</math>

Given a change in Weyl gauge <math>\widehat g_{ij} = e^{2\gamma}g_{ij}</math>, the components of the tractor bundle change according to the rule
<math display="block">\begin{bmatrix}\widehat\sigma\\\widehat \mu^i\\\widehat\rho\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}\sigma\\ \mu^i+\gamma^i\sigma\\ \rho-\gamma_j\mu^j - \gamma^2\sigma/2\end{bmatrix}</math>
where <math>\gamma_i=\nabla_i\gamma</math>, and the inverse metric <math>g^{ij}</math> has been used in one place to raise the index.  Clearly the bundle <math>\mathcal X</math> is invariant under the change in gauge, and the connection can be shown to be invariant using the conformal change in the [[Levi-Civita connection]] and Schouten tensor.

==Projective manifolds==
Let <math>M</math> be a projective manifold of dimension <math>n</math>.  Then the tractor bundle is a rank <math>n+1</math> vector bundle <math>\mathcal T</math>, with connection <math>\nabla</math>, on <math>M</math> equipped with the additional data of a line subbundle <math>\mathcal X</math> such that, for any non-vanishing local section <math>X</math> of <math>\mathcal X</math>, the linear operator
<math display="block">v\mapsto \nabla_v X\pmod{\mathcal X}</math>
is a linear isomorphism of the [[tangent space]] to <math>\mathcal T/\mathcal X</math>.<ref name="BaileyEastwoodGover"/>

One recovers an affine connection in the projective class from a section <math>X</math> of <math>\mathcal X</math> by defining
<math display="block">\nabla_{\nabla_vw}X = \nabla_v\nabla_wX \pmod{\mathcal X}</math>
and using the aforementioned isomorphism.

Explicitly, the tractor bundle can be represented in a given affine chart by pairs <math>(\mu^i\ \rho)</math>, where the connection is
<math display="block">\nabla_j\begin{bmatrix}\mu^i\\ \rho\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}\nabla_j\mu^i + \delta_j^i\rho\\ \nabla_j\rho - P_{ij}\mu^i\end{bmatrix}</math>
where <math>P_{ij}</math> is the projective Schouten tensor.  The preferred subbundle <math>\mathcal X</math> is that spanned by <math>X=(0\ 1)</math>.

Here the projective Schouten tensor of an affine connection is defined as follows.  Define the Riemann tensor in the usual way (indices are abstract)
<math display="block">(\nabla_i\nabla_j-\nabla_j\nabla_i)U^\ell = {R_{ijk}}^\ell U^k.</math>
Then
<math display="block">{R_{ijk}}^\ell = {C_{ijk}}^\ell + 2\delta^\ell_{[i}P_{j]k} + \beta_{ij}\delta_k^\ell</math>
where the Weyl tensor <math>{C_{ijk}}^\ell</math> is trace-free, and <math>2P_{[ij]} = -\beta_{ij}</math> (by Bianchi).
